QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_6

question.text: Ravi Banerjee, Manager of Krishna Debt Fund (Cat II), receives a proposal from a bloc of LPs wishing to pass a unit-holder resolution to wind up the AIF before tenure expiry. What is the MINIMUM threshold under Regulation 29 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Simple majority (51%) of investors by value.
75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF.
Unanimous consent (100%) of all unit holders.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 29 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations lists four grounds for winding up: (i) tenure expiry, (ii) trustee opinion that winding up is in investor interest, (iii) 75% of investors by VALUE passing a resolution, and (iv) SEBI direction. The LP-initiated threshold is 75% by value. The Trap: 51% is the Companies Act simple majority — not applicable. 66.67% / two-thirds is the threshold for tenure extension up to 2 years (and for change in investment strategy under CTR) — a classic adjacent-rule confusion. 100% is not required. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C asks the same threshold at all-cat. Be vigilant on XIX-D: the 2/3 tenure-extension and 3/4 winding-up thresholds are consistently swapped by test-writers.
